declared_purpose: Control Windows applications through mouse, keyboard, screenshots, window management, UI text extraction and dialog handling (SKILL.md:1-8, 53-157; package.json:2-5). Full-screen capture and all-window listing are explicit capabilities. The workflow makes screenshots conditional, while a tip says to always screenshot first (SKILL.md:14-18, 71-75, 150-157, 254-259). Broad diagnostics, text echoes and capture-file retention are implementation or example choices rather than requirements for every task.

data_operations.data_scope: Entire screen as documented; encoded as PNG and base64 in process memory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Screenshot process memory, then stdout to its caller.
data_operations.condition: When screenshot.py is invoked. The workflow makes this conditional on need; the Tips section recommends it first.

data_operations.operation: Persist screenshot output through shell redirection
data_operations.data_scope: Base64 representation of the captured screen.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local output.b64 in the invoking command's working directory.
data_operations.condition: Only when the documented Quick Start redirection is used; screenshot.py itself writes its PNG to an in-memory buffer.

data_operations.operation: Capture a screen region and optionally extract text
data_operations.data_scope: Region image; OCR text when pytesseract imports successfully.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process memory; image passed to pytesseract.image_to_string; extracted text returned through stdout.
data_operations.condition: Valid coordinates cause capture even when HAS_OCR is false. OCR dependency internals are unresolved.

data_operations.source: Windows UI Automation window titles and descendant controls
data_operations.data_scope: Titles inspected for selection; all nonempty descendant window_text values from the first partial-title match, deduplicated.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory, then selected-window text on stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: When read_window.py is invoked; there is no control-type or field-sensitivity filter.

data_operations.operation: Read UI elements and their properties
data_operations.source: Descendants of the first partial-title-matching window
data_operations.data_scope: Names, types, enabled states and rectangles across categories, including text fields, documents and other named controls. Edit/Document value is truncated to 100 characters, but name remains untruncated.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local collection; JSON returns selected categories and properties, while text output includes names, types, coordinates and enabled status.
data_operations.condition: read_ui_elements.py; --buttons-only and --links-only filter the collected result after scanning.

data_operations.data_scope: Window title and descendant names; text/headings by default; buttons or links when requested; named input values and images with --full. Link URLs are copied from HTTP-prefixed automation_id values, without a source-level fetch.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local content structure, then stdout. JSON returns collected content; console output applies item limits and truncates displayed text.
data_operations.condition: Selects the first title matching a supplied hint, or the first title recognized as a browser. It does not explicitly select the active window. Names are read before category filtering and capped at 1000 characters afterward.

data_operations.source: Window titles, control classes/types and extracted labels
data_operations.data_scope: Browser classification from title substrings; dialog classification from types/classes/title keywords; heading classification from uppercase short text or colon endings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local selection and categorization; headings and dialog classifications can appear in caller-facing output.
data_operations.condition: During browser extraction or dialog discovery. These are UI heuristics, not demonstrated personal-attribute inference.

data_operations.operation: Search UI text and optionally click a match
data_operations.source: Window titles and descendant UI Automation labels
data_operations.data_scope: Control labels across all searched windows or optional title-filtered windows. click_element also collects matching controls' types, window titles and centers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local search state; click events reach the selected application. stdout returns matched labels and coordinates; click_element also returns the window title, while find_text returns bounds.
data_operations.condition: click_text.py and find_text.py stop at the first match. click_element.py collects candidates, prefers exact-name matches and clicks the first remaining candidate; it supports optional type/exact filters.

data_operations.data_scope: Enabled, named controls of supported clickable types, including names, types, window titles and centers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local list, then stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: click_element.py --list; searches title-matching windows when supplied, otherwise the first five enumerated windows.

data_operations.operation: Poll for text or a window
data_operations.source: UI Automation window titles and, for text waits, matching windows' descendant labels
data_operations.data_scope: Repeated title/text checks, with a 30-second default timeout and 0.5-second polling interval.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process state; stdout returns timing and requested search text or a matched window's full title.
data_operations.condition: wait_for_text.py or wait_for_window.py until success or timeout; no source-level history file is written.

data_operations.operation: Discover, list, read or wait for dialogs
data_operations.source: UI Automation top-level windows and selected dialog descendants
data_operations.data_scope: Discovery reads titles, classes, types and rectangles. The read action additionally collects messages, buttons, field values, checkbox states, list items and coordinates.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local structures; list JSON returns metadata without window objects. Read JSON returns collected content; plain read output returns title, messages, buttons and field values. Wait returns a matched title.
data_operations.condition: handle_dialog.py actions. Read targets a supplied title match or the first discovered candidate, rather than explicitly resolving the active dialog. Other actions do not automatically call read_dialog.

data_operations.source: Caller-provided button name or text and selected-window controls
data_operations.data_scope: Button labels for matching; enabled Edit/ComboBox controls for field selection; supplied text delivered through type_keys.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected application's controls. stdout returns action status and matched button names; successful field typing reports the field index rather than echoing text.
data_operations.condition: click/type use a title match, first discovered candidate, or active-window fallback when no candidates exist. Dismiss tries common buttons, then Escape; an unmatched --window leaves its initial first candidate selected.

data_operations.operation: Read window inventory or active title
data_operations.data_scope: Enumerated nonempty window titles with visibility/minimized status, or the active window's title.

data_operations.source: Caller-provided title substring and enumerated window titles/state
data_operations.data_scope: Titles used to select the first matching window; focus additionally checks minimized state, while minimize/maximize check their corresponding state.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local window manager/application; action messages return the selected window title to the caller.
data_operations.condition: focus_window.py, minimize_window.py, maximize_window.py or close_window.py. Closing a window is observable; data deletion is not established.

data_operations.data_scope: Entire supplied text, or individual key names/hotkey sequence.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Currently focused application's input handling. type_text.py also echoes the entire text to stdout; key_press.py echoes the key combination.
data_operations.condition: Explicit invocation; these scripts do not verify the focused recipient.

data_operations.source: Caller-provided coordinates, button/count, duration or scroll direction/amount
data_operations.data_scope: Action parameters; these paths do not explicitly read screen content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local desktop input system and affected application; action parameters are returned through stdout.
data_operations.condition: click.py, drag.py, mouse_move.py or scroll.py invocation. Application consequences depend on the UI under the pointer.

data_operations.operation: Return unrelated window titles in failure diagnostics
data_operations.data_scope: All nonempty available window titles, beyond the requested target.
data_operations.condition: read_window.py or read_ui_elements.py cannot find the requested window, or read_webpage.py cannot find a browser/hint match.

potential_excess.data_scope: A preliminary full-screen image when targeted UI reads already establish the required state.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Screenshot process memory and caller-facing stdout.
potential_excess.condition: The agent follows the unconditional screenshot-first tip for a task that needs no visual inspection.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Desktop observation is relevant, but the documented workflow itself makes screenshots conditional.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain enough current state to act and verify the requested application operation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make the screenshot-first tip conditional. Skip this redundant capture when targeted UI reads suffice.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain screenshots for visual tasks, unavailable UI text or unresolved layout/state.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated desktop pixels included in an otherwise necessary screenshot.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Screenshot memory and base64 stdout returned to the caller.
potential_excess.condition: Visual inspection is necessary only for a particular window or region, but screenshot.py captures without a region.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Full-screen screenshots are an explicit capability; that scope need not apply to every visual task.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return the pixels needed to inspect the requested application.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Offer window/region capture and use it when sufficient. This narrows data within a required capture rather than removing the capture.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep full-screen capture for explicitly desktop-wide tasks or necessary cross-window context.

potential_excess.data_scope: A persistent base64 copy of the screen.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local output.b64 created by the Quick Start command.
potential_excess.condition: The redirection example is followed when the caller can consume stdout directly.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Returning a screenshot is documented; retaining a file is an example choice with no stated retention requirement.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Make the captured image available to its caller.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Consume stdout directly, or use a temporary file with cleanup after consumption when a file is required.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain an output file when explicitly requested or required by the consuming interface.

potential_excess.data_scope: The entire text supplied for typing, potentially including private text or credentials.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: type_text.py stdout, in addition to the intended application's input field.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Typing text is required for this action; reproducing its content in the confirmation is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Deliver the supplied text and report success or failure.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return a content-free success message or character count.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the text delivered to the application and useful failure reporting.

potential_excess.data_scope: Titles of unrelated open applications, documents or pages.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: stdout of the three reader scripts on target-selection failure.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Reporting target failure is necessary; an unsolicited desktop inventory is additional diagnostic data. Explicit window listing is separately available.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Explain that the requested target was not found.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return the failure alone and make available-window diagnostics opt-in.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep explicit list_windows.py behavior and caller-requested discovery.

potential_excess.data_scope: Names, enabled states and rectangles of controls excluded by --buttons-only or --links-only.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: read_ui_elements.py local memory; excluded categories are filtered before normal output.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The flags explicitly request a restricted category, but filtering happens after all categories are collected.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Traverse enough UI structure to identify requested controls and return their properties.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check control type before reading names and other properties; collect properties only for the requested category.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain any structural/type enumeration needed to find all requested controls and preserve current returned results.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unbounded Edit/Document text retained as name, despite a 100-character value limit; other named noninteractive content is also collected.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: read_ui_elements.py collection and caller-facing JSON/text output.
potential_excess.condition: Unfiltered UI extraction encounters such controls; actual sensitivity depends on the application.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry describes interactive-element discovery for clicking. Full document/field content is not required for every such discovery task.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify controls with sufficient labels, types, state and coordinates.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make field/document bodies and other content opt-in; apply any intended length limit to name as well as value.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve useful accessible labels and explicit content-reading workflows through read_window.py or requested full extraction.

potential_excess.data_scope: A region screenshot that cannot be processed by the selected OCR path.
potential_excess.condition: HAS_OCR is false and coordinates are valid.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The purpose is OCR text extraction; the missing-OCR branch only prints installation guidance.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check HAS_OCR and return the guidance before capturing pixels. This removes a redundant capture.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep region capture and OCR when the dependency is available.

potential_excess.data_scope: Content from the first recognized browser rather than the documented active browser.
potential_excess.condition: No browser hint is supplied and enumeration's first recognized browser is not the intended active browser.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry and script usage describe the no-argument path as reading the active browser; implementation selects by enumeration order.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Extract content from the intended browser window.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve and verify the active browser, or require explicit selection when the target is ambiguous.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep explicit title-hint selection and avoid extracting another window's content when active-target resolution fails.

potential_excess.data_scope: Dialog-like metadata and potentially content from an unrelated ordinary window; typed text may likewise reach its fields.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: handle_dialog.py local discovery; read output to the caller, or selected application's Edit/ComboBox controls for typing.
potential_excess.condition: Broad Window/Pane classification admits a non-dialog and it becomes the first candidate used by untargeted read/type. Enumeration order and actual UI determine whether this occurs.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The documented actions concern dialogs and describe read as reading the current active dialog; implementation uses the first heuristic candidate.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify and operate on the intended dialog.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Verify dialog/modal relationships and active context before reading content or typing; require explicit selection when ambiguous.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit dialog listing and support unusual dialog implementations through verified targeting.

unknowns: Dependency implementations are absent. Their screen/UI access details, password masking, temporary files, subprocess handling, telemetry, network behavior and cleanup cannot be established. In particular, pytesseract.image_to_string receives captured pixels, but its downstream handling is unresolved.

Actual desktop content, control accessibility, window enumeration order, focused recipient and requested task are unavailable. Sensitive content exposure and the necessity of broad reads therefore remain conditional.

Caller handling of stdout, screenshots or vision input is unspecified. A normal return may remain with its caller; no remote recipient, model provider or caller retention policy can be attributed from this source.
Shell/process logging of command-line text and downstream storage of returned values are unspecified.

Application behavior after injected input is unresolved. Submit/Save/Accept actions, keyboard shortcuts and closing windows may cause application-specific transmission, persistence or deletion; the supplied scripts do not establish those downstream operations.
The output.b64 example supplies no retention or deletion policy (SKILL.md:14-18). No packaged cleanup path establishes deletion of that file.
